The result of one model call

Source: R/harnessr-package.R
gr_result.Rd

Returned by hr_call(). Designed so a caller can never be handed NULL or character(0) where a string is expected. vignette("core") shows each field on a worked call.

Fields

ok

Logical(1). FALSE for transport failures, HTTP errors, and successful calls that returned no text (a refusal or content filter).

text

Character(1), always. "" when ok is FALSE. Never NULL, never character(0), and newlines are preserved.

error

Character or NULL. What went wrong, including the HTTP body for API-side errors.

usage

List with input and output token counts and their provenance: "reported" by the provider, "counted" here with the "tiktoken" tokenizer or as a zero for a request that failed or was not sent, or "estimated" with another tokenizer. reasoning and cached_input are added when the provider reports them, as parts of output and input.

status, finish_reason, retryable, model, raw

HTTP status, the API's stop reason ("length" for a reply cut off at the output cap, whatever the provider called it, and NA when the client reports none), whether a retry could help, the model id the call asked for, and the parsed response body.

cached

TRUE when the reply came from an hr_cache() or an hr_replay_client() rather than the network.

served_model, response_id, fingerprint

What the provider said about its reply: the model that answered, its response id and its system fingerprint. NA where it said nothing.

attempts

Requests sent for this reply, retries included: 0 for a reply from a cache or a recording, NA when the transport does not say.

A request the run's limits did not send (see hr_governor()) also carries refused = TRUE and the condition in refusal.

Methods

print() shows ok, the model, the token usage and either the text or the error.

See also

hr_call() which returns one, hr_client(), hr_mock_client()

hr_call(), hr_client(), hr_mock_client()

Examples

res <- hr_call(hr_mock_client(function(m, p) "hello"), "hi")
c(ok = res$ok, text = res$text)
#>      ok    text 
#>  "TRUE" "hello"
